newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London firm, Dow seen higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London firm, Dow seen higher.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly higher in London on Thursday as European investors drew comfort from Wall Street managing to finish well above its lowest levels on Wednesday.

Dealers here expect the Dow Jones industrial average to start around 20 points higher, supported by a steady bond market and firmer futures. "People are taking some comfort that the Dow clawed back from being down 130 points to just 71 points," one market maker said.
"The bonds seems to have recovered a bit so we'll probably have a nice technical bounce. But how long it will last is anyone's guess."
The March S&P 500 futures contract traded on the Globex automated market was up 2.05 points at 741.60 by 1050 GMT while the U.S. March T-bond rose 4/32 to 113-1/32.
Trading activity was thin, however as most players waited to see whether the Dow would once again prove to be resilient.
"This market is just too difficult to call at the moment. We've been fooled before so it doesn't really pay to take any chances," another trader said.
Ahead of the Dow's 1430 GMT start, the market is expected to focus on U.S. consumer price (CPI) and retail sales numbers, due at 1330 GMT.
The November CPI is forecast to show a monthly rise of 0.3 percent, unchanged from the previous month, while retail sales are expected to increase by 0.3 percent month-on-month.

WMX Technologies was up $3/4 at $36-3/8 after a group led by international financier George Soros said on Wednesday in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing that it held a 5.2 percent stake in the waste management company.
"Some people think Soros will try and get better value for shareholders which has helped a bit today," one dealer said.
Elsewhere, Intel, which soared $7-3/4 on Wednesday was up another $3/8 at $137-1/4.

Press reports that Hollywood power player Michael Ovitz has talked with Sony in recent weeks about taking a top job with the electronics giant hit Disney, down $1/2 at $71-3/4. Ovitz has been Disney's No. 2 for just a year.
